productQualityProblem: The incumbent shows substantial stochastic-output instability on admitted short-event train text: 39.84% unstable rows on Hippocorpus and 28.13% on Unexpected Events across five dropout passes. Prior hard pseudo-label and valence adaptations increased deterministic false positives.
hypothesis: Softly anchoring two stochastic student passes to the frozen incumbent's deterministic probabilities while directly minimizing their disagreement can improve short-event representation stability without hard-label sharpening or changing the classifier head.

data.pool: same deterministic 5274-row 1:1 Hippocorpus/Unexpected Events train pool used by selective-consensus feasibility
data.labels: none; frozen incumbent soft probabilities are research teacher targets, not gold
data.validation: prepared participant-disjoint validation splits remain untouched until candidate exists

fixedTraining.updates: top two encoder layers only; Product-18 classifier head frozen tensor-identical
fixedTraining.loss: mean soft BCE of two dropout passes against deterministic teacher probabilities on Product-18 plus unit-weight probability MSE between the two passes

successCriteria.independentDropoutStability: on both previously untouched validations unstable-row percentage must not increase, mean pairwise exact-output agreement must not decrease, and average relative unstable-row reduction across sources must be >=20%
successCriteria.historicalDevelopment: micro-F1 >=0.528052805280528, false positives <=58, false negatives <=85, and no supported-label F1 regression worse than 0.05
successCriteria.shortSlice: micro-F1 regression no worse than 0.02 and false positives <=5
successCriteria.deterministicUnlabeledBehavior: candidate/incumbent exact-output agreement >=0.85 and each 0/1/2 distribution shift <=0.08 on both validations
successCriteria.decision: RETAIN_FOR_RESEARCH only if all guards pass; otherwise REJECT
